ai_panel_section_help: Connect AI apps to Birkly or chat inside the admin.
ai_panel_https_title: Claude requires an HTTPS Connector URL
ai_panel_https_body: Claude, ChatGPT, and Cursor reject http:// connector URLs. Open Birkly using https:// on a public address, then copy the Connector URL shown here. HTTP and localhost URLs will not work in Claude.
ai_panel_localhost_desc: How AI connects when Birkly runs on localhost — without exposing admin insecurely.
ai_panel_localhost_li_assistant: Built-in assistant / Ollama on localhost — OK (outbound BYOAI or http://localhost:11434).
ai_panel_localhost_li_remote: Remote connectors (Claude / ChatGPT / Cursor cloud) need a public HTTPS Connector URL — plain http://localhost/mcp is rejected.
ai_panel_localhost_li_bridge: mcp-bridge recipe — local stdio bridge for desktop AI tools: open mcp-bridge.js (also under Developer / debug below).
ai_panel_localhost_li_tunnel: Tunnel recipe — cloudflared or ngrok → HTTPS → your local /mcp, then paste that HTTPS URL as the Connector URL.
ai_panel_localhost_security_help: Keep security warnings on: do not expose the admin panel to the public internet as a default. Prefer mcp-bridge or a short-lived tunnel.
ai_panel_migration_body: Existing service agents are admin-only until you assign roles or users. Edit each service agent's Who can use settings to share access.
ai_panel_personal_desc: Connect Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor with your own Birkly permissions. Every team member uses the same URL but signs in with their own account.
ai_panel_service_intro: Shared AI connections with a fixed CMS role. Only admins can create service agents.
ai_panel_assistant_desc: Chat with AI inside Birkly using your provider API key.
ai_panel_dev_lead: For local development only. Not needed for normal setup.
ai_panel_dev_bridge: mcp-bridge.js — local development helper for Claude Desktop (advanced only).
ai_panel_assistant_modal_intro: Connect an AI provider for the in-admin chat button. You need a developer API key — consumer subscriptions (ChatGPT Plus, Claude Pro) do not include API access.
ai_panel_api_url_hint: API endpoint URL (required for custom providers)
ai_panel_ollama_body: No API key needed. Make sure Ollama is running (default: http://localhost:11434).
ai_panel_models_help: Models are loaded live from your provider. Search the list or type a model ID.
ai_panel_mcp_type_legend: What type of agent do you need?
ai_panel_mcp_type_personal_desc: Each user connects with their own Birkly role and permissions. One shared URL for the whole team.
ai_panel_mcp_type_service_desc: A shared bot that always acts as a specific CMS role (e.g. always editor). You choose who can use it.
ai_panel_mcp_personal_intro: The personal connector is already set up for your site. Copy its URL and paste it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor — each team member signs in with their own account.
ai_panel_mcp_service_intro: Create a shared service agent with a fixed CMS role. Choose who can see and connect to it.
ai_panel_mcp_presets_help: Site builder uses the Admin role so connected AI can read and write project/ HTML, CSS, and JS alongside CMS content.
ai_panel_mcp_role_help_tip: Viewer = read only. Editor = suggest changes (often needs your approval). Admin = full access. This role applies to everyone who connects to this service agent.
ai_panel_mcp_who_can_use_help: Admins always see all service agents. Select roles and/or individual users who may connect.
ai_panel_mcp_visible_roles_aria: Roles that can use this agent
ai_panel_mcp_allowed_users_aria: Users that can use this agent
ai_panel_mcp_approvals_note: Write approvals are handled in the AI app that connects (e.g. Claude tool permissions), not in Birkly.
ai_panel_mcp_created_body: Copy the Connector URL and paste it in your AI app. Leave Client ID and Client Secret empty.
hosting_wizard_val_same_host_project: CMS and public share {host}. With “Root / opens admin”, the bundled site is served at /project/.
hosting_wizard_val_cms_no_admin: CMS URL should be the site origin only (https://{host}), not …/admin.
hosting_wizard_val_alias_overlap: "{alias}" is on both CMS and public alias lists. Requests resolve as CMS — remove it from public aliases.
